content:
mira: Heads-up 11: we need to finalize SLA credit mechanics and the exact legal-friendly clause for GA. Legal wants deterministic language.
leila: quick ask 12: do we want credits as % of monthly invoice or fixed USD per outage minute? both have ops implications.
ethan: ops preference is % of monthly invoice. simpler to calculate and scales with customer spend.
carmen: legal: % is fine but clause must include measurement windows and exclusions (maintenance, customer misconfig, force majeure). I'll draft.
sam: SRE note: measurement windows we recommend: availability measured monthly per-region, with synthetic checks every 1m. Use 99.95% monthly uptime as baseline.
mira: okay assume 99.95 baseline. what's the credit table we propose?
leila: draft table (proposal):
1) 99.95% - 99.9% -> 5% credit of monthly invoice
2) 99.9% - 99.0% -> 15% credit
3) < 99.0% -> 35% credit + optional exit right after 30 days notice
ethan: exit right is huge; legal will push back. maybe replace with escalation + onboarding support instead of auto-exit.
carmen: agree. we'll avoid automatic exit. propose instead: below 99.0% -> 35% credit + dedicated SRE engagement for 30 days.
mira: sounds reasonable. add a clause: credits are sole and exclusive remedy.
legal-bot: Suggestion: include a clear definition of "Downtime" and a calculation example. Also add exclusions: scheduled maintenance >= 48h notice, DDoS under mitigation, customer-side network failures.
leila: can someone paste the outage credit calc example? want to include in the SLA appendix.
sam: example calc snippet:```
monthly_period_seconds = 30 * 24 * 3600
outage_seconds = sum(unhealthy_intervals)
availability = (monthly_period_seconds - outage_seconds) / monthly_period_seconds
credit = lookup_credit_percentage(availability) * monthly_invoice_amount
```
ethan: we'll need a short reproducible example for a 45-minute outage:
leila: 45 minutes -> outage_seconds = 2700
availability = (2592000 - 2700)/2592000 = 99.895% -> falls in 99.95-99.9? actually that's 99.895 < 99.9 so 5% credit per draft.
carmen: wording note: use "availability" rather than "uptime" in legal text. less ambiguous.
mira: ops question: who signs off on scheduled maintenance window SLA offsets? e.g., planned upgrades.
sam: ops: scheduled maintenance is excluded if >48h notice provided and we publish the window. we track it in the incident calendar and exclude those seconds from outage_seconds.
leila: pricing impact: ravi isn't here but we should estimate worst-case credits for runway. We need a risk bucket in FinOps for credits up to X% of ARR.
mira: action: leila -> coordinate with finance for a one-pager risk calc. due EOD tomorrow.
carmen: legal action: I'll drop a redline with the exact clause phrases: definition of availability, exclusions, calculation, sole remedy language, and dedicated-engagement wording. ETA: tomorrow noon.
sam: monitoring action: confirm synthetic measurement points (global regions). can we list regions?
ethan: yes: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1. synthetics run from each region once per minute. we'll publish the raw checks for transparency.
leila: support playbook linkage: we should add an SLA appendix that maps credit thresholds to support tiers (who to call, escalation path). I'll draft mapping: 1) 5% -> tier-2; 2) 15% -> assign infra lead; 3) 35% -> exec escalation + dedicated SRE.
mira: good. also include a communication timeline: acknowledge outage in 15m, incident report in 72h, root cause analysis in 7 days.
carmen: legal: we can commit to FR timelines but keep "reasonably promptly" for some items. will propose concrete commitments for those three items.
sam: operational nuance: we will not credit for partial degradation (e.g., increased latency) unless it causes failed requests > threshold. define error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 10m as service-impacting.
leila: we should include a note for early-access customers: offer a one-time waiver/discount in exchange for telemetry and post-launch beta feedback.
mira: marketing ask: can we offer a short-term GA promo: 2 months free for first-year enterprise customers? that affects credit exposure. need finance input.
ethan: tech note: we must ensure our billing pipeline can ingest credit adjustments automatically. that's a sprint item for billing team.
mira: final call: owners for docs + legal + ops + finance? leila: pricing liaison; carmen: legal; sam: SRE/monitoring; ethan: rollout/ops; mira: product owner. confirm.
leila: confirmed. carmen: confirmed. sam: confirmed. ethan: confirmed. legal-bot: Reminder: link to SLA template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/legal/sla-template.
mira: OK I'll take these redlines and produce the internal SLA doc and an enterprise one-pager. aim: have final wording for engineering sign-off by Friday. any objections?
leila: none.
carmen: none.
sam: none but we need test harness for synthetic transparency (I'll open ticket).
mira: thanks all, will follow up with an updated draft and a short review meeting. :white_check_mark:
